articles.title: AI startup founded by two Irish YC alumni gets backing from Stripe's Collison brothers
Exclusive: Stripe founders and Paul Graham back AI agent swarm startup Hoplite with $5.5m

brief.essentiel: Paul Graham, the Y Combinator co-founder, said the two young Irish entrepreneurs reminded him of Patrick and John Collison, the Irish brothers who founded and run the $160bn payment giant Stripe.
points: Ryan Morrissey and Bence Redmond, the co-founders of AI startup Hoplite , might not be brothers but, like the Collison brothers, are Irish, have ties to Limerick, and attended Y Combinator.
During their time at Y Combinator, Morrissey says they biked all over San Francisco to set users up for their startup, over 240 rides, a tactic Graham called the “Collison installation”.
Morrissey met Redmond at the University of Limerick and dropped out at 19, before the pair joined YC’s summer 2026 batch.
Hoplite, founded in 2026 and based in San Francisco and Dublin, is a startup that is trying to make it easier for software teams to run several AI coding agents at once.

articles.title: Startup ecosystem calls to withdraw and re-table EU Inc proposal, Isomorphic Labs bags $5B, and inside Plural's €1B fund

brief.essentiel: This week, we tracked more than 65 tech funding deals worth over €6 billion and over 4 exits, M&A transactions, rumours , and related news stories across Europe.
points: This week, I've gone straight from the scale and intensity of Slush in Helsinki to Yerevan, Armenia, where a much different startup ecosystem is taking shape.

While conversations at Slush centred on scaling European tech companies, unlocking institutional capital and removing regulatory barriers, Armenia is focused on building the foundations of a globally competitive startup ecosystem where previously diaspora has been its main competitive advantage.

AI is a common thread, but the conversations are markedly different — from infrastructure, commercialisation and technological sovereignty in Helsinki to the opportunities AI presents for smaller ecosystems to compete on the global stage.
The free, open-access Tech.eu Funding Explorer offers deeper insights into funding rounds, investor activity, company profiles and market trends.

articles.title: Following €1 billion funding round, Quantum Systems commits over €10 million to expand drone support in Ukraine

brief.essentiel: Quantum Systems and Frontline Robotics will commit more than €10 million to Ukraine to strengthen long-term support capacity for unmanned systems – arriving amid over €1.8 billion in European DefenceTech financing reported by EU-Startups in 2026.
points: This expansion comes amid wider European DefenceTech investment: EU-Startups identified more than €1.8 billion in financing across 22 startups during 2026 as of October , including Finland’s ICEYE (€450 million), Estonia’s Frankenburg Technologies (€30 million) and Germany’s INLEAP Photonics (€20 million).
The commitment follows several years of expansion by Quantum Systems, which raised €63.6 million in a 2023 Series B before securing €160 million and a further €180 million in 2025.

In 2026, the company added a €150 million financing package in February and a €1 billion Series D in July , while extending its activities beyond aerial systems through acquisitions and industrial partnerships.

The joint venture is expanding its industrial cooperation through a programme for long-term support capacity in Ukraine aimed at systems developed by Frontline Robotics and produced in Germany by Quantum Frontline Industries (QFI).

articles.title: Archer raises €9.1 million to deploy AI recruiting agents for employers and job seekers

brief.essentiel: Archer (formerly hackajob) , a London- and New York-based AI recruiting agent that works for both recruiters and job seekers, has raised €9.1 million ($10 million) in a new funding round.
points: The company has now raised more than €41.06 million ($45 million) in total since it was founded in 2014, with backers including Foresight Ventures and Techstars.

However, it faces growing competition in the AI recruitment space; London-based Jack & Jill, which also puts AI agents on both sides of the hiring table, raised €34.68 million Series A to scale its AI agents for jobseekers and employers.
The round was led by Volition Capital, with participation from existing investor AVP.

articles.title: UK startup Clarity Sensors receives €2.2 million NIHR award to make advanced medical imaging more accessible

brief.essentiel: Cambridge-based semiconductor startup Clarity Sensors has secured a €2.2 million to support the development of a new generation of photon-counting CT detectors designed to make advanced medical imaging more affordable and accessible to hospitals.
points: In the UK, Bristol-based Siloton secured a €9.98 million Innovate UK contract to develop portable retinal imaging systems, while Nottingham-based Cerca Magnetics raised €4.3 million to scale its quantum-based brain imaging technology.
London-based MintNeuro also secured €4.4 million for specialised neural-device semiconductors, while Belgium’s SamanTree Medical received €20 million in EIB financing for real-time surgical imaging.

Together, these announcements represent approximately €38.7 million in disclosed financing, rising to €40.9 million including the full Clarity Sensors project award, across a mixture of private investment, public contracts, research awards and debt financing.

The startup will lead the three-year project, known as PICASO, receiving €1.5 million (£1.3 million) of the total award, with the remaining funding allocated to the Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC) Technology Department.
